policy: Structural budget for scripts/check-architecture.mjs. Every number in `rules` is a ratchet: the script fails when an actual value exceeds it and warns when the actual value is lower (that means the budget can be lowered). `--update` only ever lowers a number; raising one is a reviewed edit of this file. `stage` is the phase this tree is being reviewed at and `terminalStage` is the one it must arrive at: when they are equal the gate forbids **any** `fileLength` exception, **any** non-zero `violations` field and any surviving `p7Todo` entry, so the terminal state cannot be declared while its exemptions still exist. At P7 the only surviving allowance is the `godCtxParams.entries` list (the orchestration entries and their private helpers, each with its file and reason).
p7Todo: Split the src/runtime/fsm.ts transition table into data files so the file drops under the 600-line limit, then delete its fileLength exception (the last exemption in this budget).
Move client/src/styles.ts's `const CSS = ` out of script scope (the last `@ts-expect-error`, `until: P7` in types/any-allowlist.json) so `node scripts/check-types.mjs --stage P7 --strict` is green.
Bump `stage` to `P7`; check-architecture.mjs then refuses to run with any exemption left.

src/runtime/fsm.ts.reason: The explicit transition table plus its guards: one table on purpose (design-arch §2.3), because splitting it would scatter the FSM's proof. P7 terminal: the table moves to data files and this exception is deleted.

entries.reason: The connect entry point: it owns the one-time inputs, the retry budget reset and the log boundary, then hands the same context to startConnectPromise, which re-enters the six-slice pipeline.
The Reconnect button: dispatch (five slices) plus startConnectPromise (six), so it is the orchestration context by construction, not by convenience.
The re-attach entry: it publishes reattach.requested and hands its context to runReattach, which spans all six slices (registry rewrite, tunnel, verify, token store).

The re-attach body: re-reads the remote state, rewrites the run registry with RemoteDeps, saves the token with Store and publishes through Reporter; splitting it would thread six parameters for no behavior change.
The restart entry: ctx.init() needs Store, the ownership proof needs Transport+RemoteDeps, and it hands the context to runRestart.
The restart body: ownership proof, foreign-conflict prompt, stop/start, registry rewrite, tunnel and verify read the same six slices as the entry point.
The explicit stop entry: ctx.init() (Store), the ownership proof (Transport+RemoteDeps) and the dispatch that owns the state write (five slices) together cover all six.
Private pipeline helper: it starts connectPipeline in the background and keeps the promise off the rejection path; the six slices come from the pipeline it calls.
Private retry helper: it dispatches connect.requested (five slices) and its run hook re-enters startConnectPromise, so the sixth slice (Store) is transitive.
Private timer callback around reconnectNow; it reads only Reporter itself but must pass the orchestration context the retry re-entry needs.
Private close listener: it publishes transport.closed through the effect owner (five slices) and arms scheduleReconnect, whose callback re-enters the pipeline; narrowing it does not compile.
Private dial helper: it reads Config/Transport/Reporter/Store itself, but hands the context to watchTransport, whose close listener re-enters the pipeline, so the parameter cannot be narrowed.

The workflow body itself: SSH, probe, managed Node, adopt/conflict, start, tunnel, verify and the store writes it ends with genuinely need Transport, RemoteDeps, Reporter, Config, Store and the guards' HostState.
Private retry-policy helper: it reads HostState (disposed) and Config (settings) and calls retryNow, which carries the orchestration context.
Host CRUD, not an orchestration entry: deleting a host dispatches host.removed (the effect owner needs the watchdog's five slices) and removes the store record and the saved secret (Store).
Settings write: persisting needs Store, and restarting the heartbeat of every connected host needs the watchdog's five slices, which together are the whole context.
